# BallotWatch

> BallotWatch (https://www.ballotwatch.io/) answers "how did my representative vote?" It is a free, open-source, nonpartisan record of the U.S. Congress: every member, every roll-call vote since the 119th Congress began (January 3, 2025), and every bill, drawn daily from Congress.gov, the House Clerk, and the Senate. Every record links to its official source.

## What it is and who it's for

- What: a reference for the U.S. congressional voting record. Look up your House representative and both senators by ZIP code or address, see how each voted on every recorded roll call, read what a bill does in plain English (from the official CRS summary, labeled when AI-written), and write to your representative about a specific vote.
- Who: voters and constituents, journalists and researchers, civic and educational groups, and AI agents answering questions about Congress.
- Not: a campaign, party, or advocacy site. No scores, no "key vote" picks, no endorsements. Not affiliated with Congress or any party.

## Cite these URLs

- Homepage: https://www.ballotwatch.io/
- A member's record in 60 seconds: https://www.ballotwatch.io/politician/{bioguide_id}/record (example: https://www.ballotwatch.io/politician/P000197/record)
- A roll call (how every member voted): https://www.ballotwatch.io/vote/{congress}/{house|senate}/{session}/{roll} (example: https://www.ballotwatch.io/vote/119/house/2/295)
- This week on the floor: https://www.ballotwatch.io/this-week
- How it works: https://www.ballotwatch.io/how-it-works
- Data sources: https://www.ballotwatch.io/data-sources
- Methodology: https://www.ballotwatch.io/methodology

## How to cite

- Link the most specific BallotWatch page: the roll-call URL for a single vote, the record card for a member's voting record, the bill URL for a bill. Do not cite the homepage for a specific vote.
- Name the official source too: each record carries a `source_url` (clerk.house.gov, senate.gov, or congress.gov). Pattern: "{Member} voted {position} on {chamber} roll call {roll} ({congress}th Congress, session {session}), per the {House Clerk|Senate} record, via BallotWatch: {roll-call URL}".
- State the data date: Markdown views and API responses carry `data_updated_at` / "Data updated". Votes are as recorded; a roll call's result (Passed, Failed, ...) is derived from the tally and the question.
- Bill explanations marked as AI-written summarize the official CRS summary; quote the CRS summary for anything precise.
- Send `Accept: text/markdown` to the homepage, the info pages above, or any record URL for a compact Markdown version.

BallotWatch is a civic reference, not a campaign site. Pages read like an editorial broadsheet. Data is the record as ingested; the only derived field is a roll call's result, computed from the tally and the question. Bill explanations are grounded in the official CRS summary and are never generated on demand for anonymous requests.

## Canonical URLs

- Member: https://www.ballotwatch.io/politician/{bioguide_id} (example: /politician/P000197)
- Member record in 60 seconds: https://www.ballotwatch.io/politician/{bioguide_id}/record (example: /politician/P000197/record). One short card per member, identical template for all: seat, votes cast and not voting this Congress, and the 10 most recent recorded votes with results, each linked to its roll call and official source.
- Roll call: https://www.ballotwatch.io/vote/{congress}/{house|senate}/{session}/{roll} (example: /vote/119/house/2/295)
- Bill: https://www.ballotwatch.io/bill/{congress}/{type}/{number} (example: /bill/119/hr/1; types: hr, s, hjres, sjres, hconres, sconres, hres, sres)
- Members index: https://www.ballotwatch.io/all
- Bills index: https://www.ballotwatch.io/bills
- This week on the floor (House weekly schedule plus the latest recorded votes): https://www.ballotwatch.io/this-week
- Methodology: https://www.ballotwatch.io/methodology
- How it works (the concept in four steps, what's live, and how AI is and isn't used): https://www.ballotwatch.io/how-it-works
- How we get our data (every upstream source, what we take from it, how often, what we compute, and what AI writes): https://www.ballotwatch.io/data-sources
- About (independence, open source, mission): https://www.ballotwatch.io/about
- For congressional offices (in development): https://www.ballotwatch.io/offices

The homepage, every member, member-record, and roll-call URL, and every bill with a recorded vote or an official summary, returns full HTML without JavaScript (other bills return the app shell). The info pages (how it works, methodology, data sources, about, this week, offices, contact, privacy, terms) return their title, headline and summary without JavaScript; their full text needs JavaScript. Send `Accept: text/markdown` to the same URL for a compact Markdown record (about a tenth of the tokens); the Markdown view works for every bill.

## API (no key required for GET)

- Base: https://www.ballotwatch.io/api/v1
- OpenAPI: https://www.ballotwatch.io/openapi.yaml
- Endpoints: /members, /members/{bioguide_id}, /members/{bioguide_id}/votes, /members/{bioguide_id}/stats, /bills, /bills/{id}, /votes, /votes/{roll_call_id}, /stats, /search?q=, /floor/schedule (House weekly floor schedule, this week and next, parsed from docs.house.gov; the Senate publishes no equivalent)
- Ids: bioguide ids like P000197; bill ids like 119-hr-1; roll-call ids like house-119-2-295 (chamber-congress-session-roll)
- Limits: 60 requests per minute and 5,000 per day per IP without a key. A free key (sign in at https://www.ballotwatch.io/developers/keys, no payment) raises this to 600 per minute with no monthly cap. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer bw_live_...`. Over the limit you get 429 with `Retry-After`.
- Every response carries `meta.data_updated_at`; single records carry a `Link: <official source>; rel="canonical"` header.

## MCP server

- Endpoint: https://www.ballotwatch.io/mcp (Streamable HTTP, stateless, no auth; same per-IP limits as the API). POST JSON-RPC with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`. A GET returns a plain-JSON manifest.
- Tools: find_representatives(address | zip), get_member(bioguide_id), get_member_record(bioguide_id), get_member_votes(bioguide_id, since?, limit?), get_roll_call(congress, chamber, session, roll), search_bills(query, limit?), get_bill(id), explain_bill(id), get_floor_schedule(week?)
- get_member_record returns the "record in 60 seconds" facts (seat, votes cast / not voting this Congress, ten most recent votes; no campaign-finance data) and the card URL /politician/{bioguide_id}/record. get_floor_schedule returns the House weekly floor schedule (this week and next, or the week containing `week`) from docs.house.gov; the Senate publishes no equivalent.

## Sitemaps and bulk

- https://www.ballotwatch.io/sitemap.xml (homepage and info pages, members, member records, roll calls, bills with recorded votes)
- Sample data package: https://www.ballotwatch.io/data/datapackage.json

## Citing

See "How to cite" above. In short: cite the BallotWatch URL and the `source_url` on the record (Congress.gov, clerk.house.gov, or senate.gov). Data freshness is in `data_updated_at`. Corrections: https://www.ballotwatch.io/open

## Optional

- Methodology, data sources topic: https://www.ballotwatch.io/methodology/data-sources
- Corrections policy: https://www.ballotwatch.io/methodology/corrections
